Chapter 7: Moving Beyond Games — The Power of Authentic Transactions
Now that you’ve started to recognize those underlying patterns in how we interact, what comes next? Well, it’s about taking that brave step beyond old games, and learning how to have truly authentic, adult-to-adult conversations.
Think of it this way — it’s like stepping off a stage, leaving the script behind, and having a real, unscripted conversation with the people around you. No more hiding behind roles or familiar lines.
Authentic transactions are all about being open and honest, really showing up in the moment. Instead of falling back on old habits or secret agendas, both people speak directly — sharing their needs, feelings, and boundaries without any hidden motives or manipulation.
I’ll be honest, this kind of openness can feel a bit scary at first, especially if you’re used to the comfort of playing familiar games. But here’s the thing — it’s also incredibly freeing. When you interact from that adult part of yourself, you make room for real understanding and genuine connection.
So, how do you put this into practice? Let me share a few practical tools to help you foster more authentic transactions:
First, try naming your feelings and needs out loud. Instead of dropping hints or slipping into a role, just say what you feel and what you need, clearly and directly.
Next, focus on listening actively. That means really tuning in to the other person’s perspective, rather than getting ready to defend yourself or launch a counterattack.
Another helpful habit? Pause before you react. Take a breath and ask yourself — which part of me is about to respond here?
And finally, invite collaboration. If there’s a challenge, try framing it as something you both can tackle together, instead of a battle you have to win.
Let’s make this real with an example. Imagine someone who usually falls into the “Why Don’t You—Yes But” game. Instead of playing along, they might say, “I’m feeling stuck and unsure what to do. I’d appreciate your ideas, but I also notice I tend to dismiss suggestions. Can we talk about that?”
That kind of honesty stops the game in its tracks and invites a whole new conversation.
Over time, practicing these authentic transactions builds trust, and makes relationships stronger and more resilient. Even more, it helps you develop a solid sense of self — one that’s not tied to old scripts or outdated roles.
